findings.summary: Four measured numbers in the scene 123 registry comment were wrong, in a comment whose own text asserted it had been read back off report-*.json rather than remembered. An exhaustive grep of the whole tree -- including .cache, dist, native/build-* and a sibling worktree -- found those four figures nowhere as measurements, and the file mtimes showed the comment predated the reports it cited by eight seconds: it was written from a stream summary and the reports were then regenerated by a later parity run. The SDL_GPU and Dawn values were also inverted, and 'within1 100% on both' was false on both (5 and 4 pixels exceed one count). Rewritten as a plain table of figures, each labelled with the file it came from.

Two superlatives were refuted by the same file that carried them. 'The family's widest band' -- scene 126's Dawn row, in a table two lines above, is 1.7e-3 at max 18 against scene 123's 8.6e-4 at max 1. And 'thresholds two orders above the band' -- 0.003/7.6e-4 and 0.007/8.6e-4 are 3.9x and 8.1x, under one order; the phrasing had been copied from the scene 125 paragraph where it does hold. Both replaced with the arithmetic.

The browser-vs-browser figure was given as 8.9e-4 with no artifact behind it. Recomputed with the repo's own comparator over the two committed PNGs: 0.0008818. Corrected, and the comment now names the recompute path instead of implying a stored artifact.

`loader:splat`'s provenance gained a line naming `load-spz.ts#loadSPZ`, which non-SPZ scenes never compile -- and the dedicated `loader:splat-spz` row already carried that exact string. Verified in the generated tree: scene 120's feature-activation.json listed the module under an active row while the next row said 'not reached', and scene 120 emits no load_spz at all. That is precisely the drift the provenance field exists to detect, shipped to all nine splat scenes. Reverted to the one row that owns it.

`load_spz`'s definition was gated on `spzReached` while its provenance suffix was gated on `spzRotation !== undefined`. The reverse of the refused combination would stamp a provenance line naming a module onto a file containing none of it. Not reachable today, but the file's own doc says the definition and the call cannot disagree; one word aligns them.

The colour fold's comment argued the change entirely through `setPbrUnlit`, but `staticColor3Value` has FOUR sinks and they split two ways. The unlit tint and the two subsurface options fail on undefined, so for them this is refusal-to-acceptance and cannot move a scene. `setPbrEmissive` and the sheen colour are VALUE sinks that omit the field rather than refusing, so a colour that used to default -- black for emissive, absent for sheen -- now folds into the composed variant. Measured before shipping: the three corpus scenes reaching either sink regenerate byte-identically, because scene 20's emissive channels are runtime randoms and still refuse. The comment now names all four sinks and the split, and a test covers the value sink specifically, because that is where the neutrality proof is load-bearing rather than a formality.

docs/fidelity.md gave the probe's baseline as a single 0.00131 when the two backends publish 0.0013155 and 0.0012905, and did not say that the probe ran at an earlier build stamp than the parity numbers beside it. Both stated.

`packageSpz` is not bake-cached, and the stated reason -- that a replay would skip its four contract assertions -- does not hold: the cache key already covers the pin, the packager's own compiled source and the input bytes, so a hit implies the same run those contracts passed.
findings.blockedBy: The reviewer is right that the reason is wrong, and caching it would save the measured 283 ms against a 19 ms replay on every recompile reaching loadSPZ. But the rotation is an OBSERVED fact that must ride along in the cached payload, which means extending the 12-byte frame the parse already carries and re-versioning it -- a change to the cache format, on the same branch that just re-versioned it once for the harmonics sidecar. Two format bumps in one branch is how a stale entry gets unframed as a header. It wants its own change with its own version bump.
findings.filedIn: src/splat-packager.ts, with the real reason now stated in place of the wrong one

findings.summary: The new cross-kind splat refusal re-implements an output-collision check the same file already owns forty lines below, and misses the `basis`-vs-`texture` pair on a URL ending .ktx.
findings.blockedBy: The general fix is to build the asset record first and refuse on an output collision, which is the idiom already there -- but that reorders registration for every asset kind, and the collision it would newly catch is one no corpus scene reaches. Reordering asset registration under a scene wave, to catch a case nothing exercises, is the kind of change that wants its own before/after over all 243 trees.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, folded into the splat entry

findings.summary: `typedArrayStem` is a third copy of the same seven-arm table in one file, and its docstring names the second (`cppType`) as though it already read from it.
findings.blockedBy: Collapsing `cppType` and `typeKey` onto the stem is mechanical and emission-neutral, but it touches the data model's type spelling for every typed array in the compiler, on a branch whose neutrality proof is already carrying a value-sink change. It belongs with its own whole-tree diff rather than inside this one.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, folded into the restated-body inventory entry

findings.summary: `importPinnedModuleFetching` is a fourth near-identical pinned importer, and its docstring argues against the wrong neighbour -- the function it resembles is `importPinnedModuleUnasynced`, not `importPinnedModuleWithExports`.
findings.blockedBy: The real reason it cannot reuse the closest sibling is the unasync transform: loadSPZ genuinely awaits DecompressionStream, so assertPinnedSync would trip. That reason is now stated where the docstring was wrong. Collapsing all four behind one shadowed-import helper is worth doing when a fifth arrives; at four, with one genuine behavioural difference between them, the helper's option bag would carry more conditions than the duplication costs.
findings.filedIn: src/pinned-shader-composer.ts, with the real reason stated

findings.summary: An observed rotation cannot see a per-container fork: a pin that grew a version-conditional rotation would be observed correctly for the one container a scene loads and emitted as a scene-wide constant.
findings.blockedBy: The belt is one more assertion -- refuse if the pinned rotation write sits under a branch -- and the lowerer already reads that declaration for its attachParsedSplat contract. It is not a defect today (load-spz.js writes it unconditionally at the end of loadSPZ) and adding a shape assertion for a fork the pin does not have would be guessing at its future shape rather than pinning its present one.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, folded into the splat entry

findings.summary: Scene 114 is not integrated: two of its contracts shipped here, and the rest is a subsystem.
findings.blockedBy: Deliberate, and the reason is the finding: with the four compile-level blockers stubbed the scene builds CLEAN, but the pin hands its deform projection to the basic pick pipeline too and the scene's morph-only quad needs the noskin-morph arm -- neither of which any compile error reports. The browser composes six pick modules for this scene against this port's two. Landing it would have shipped a wrong picture with a green build: the quad's bind pose is at x = -1.65 and its posed position at x = -0.30, and the scan region covers only the posed one, so the marker would vanish rather than shift.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md, folded into the GPU-picking entry with the capture path
